title: Annotatio V §.III close: Neoterici make Oral fundamental; Tertullian twist; Mayer on Spener — stop before §.IV
pass_a_gloss: Nay most of the Lutherans’ Neoterics — and among them a certain Wittenberger — fight gravely not only for the truth of the Triple of eating, but also for its necessity to salvation, certainly for the Fundamentality of the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body in relation to the Christian faith, crying that whoever deny the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body — even with the Supernatural and Spiritual most earnestly built up — dissent fundamentally alike from them and from the Christian faith, although it is altogether unheard in Scripture and the primitive Church, and extorted only from one saying of Tertullian, partly obscure, partly equivocal, partly finally Rhetorical — (Flesh is fed with Christ’s Body and blood, that the soul also may be fattened from God. Book on the Resurrection) — by Bajer’s little strings, Compend. Theolog. Historic. p. 586 beginning; concerning which Tertullian yet what is to be thought, and in what place his Authority is to be held, even most lately the Theologian of most celebrated name and honor Joh. Frid. Mayer not obscurely hints, when he judges Philipp. Jacob. Spener of pious memory — wondrously hated by the greatest part of the Lutheran Church — rightly to be called the Tertullian of our age, Bibliothec. Scriptor. Theologiæ Moralis, p. 27.
pass_b_english: §.III close: many Lutheran Neoterics (a Wittenberger among them) fight not only for the triple’s truth but for Oral’s necessity and fundamentality to Christian faith — branding deniers of Oral (even with spiritual stressed) as fundamental dissenters.

The Oral claim is unheard in Scripture and the primitive Church, and is twisted from one partly rhetorical Tertullian line (Bajer, Compend. p. 586); Mayer hints Spener is rightly called our age’s Tertullian (Bibl. Theol. Mor. p. 27). Stop before §.IV.
source_text: Quin Neoterici Lutheranorum plurimi, hosque inter Wittebergensis quidam, non pro veritate duntaxat Trigæ manducationis, sed & pro necessitate ejusdem ad salutem, certè pro Fundamentalitate Oralis Corporis Christi Manducationis, in relatione ad fidem Christianam, graviter depugnant, fundamentaliter à se pariter atque à fide Christiana dissidere, clamitando, quotquot Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem, Supernaturali licèt Spiritualique enixissimè adstructa, inficiantur, utut in Scriptura & primitiva Ecclesia prorsus inauditam, & nonnisi ex unius Tertulliani dictione hac, partim obscura, partim æquivoca, partim denique Rhetorica: (Caro, Corpore & sanguine Christi vescitur, ut & anima de Deo saginetur. Libro de Resurrectione) Bajerianis fidiculis Compend. Theolog. Historic. p. 586. initio, extortum, de quo tamen Tertulliano quid sentiendum, quóve locô hujus Auctoritas habenda sit, vel novissimè Celeberrimi nominis honorisque Theologus Joh. Frid. Mayerus, haud obscurè subinnuit, quando piæ memoriæ Philipp. Jacob. Spenerum, Lutheranæ Ecclesiæ parti maximæ mirè exosum, nostræ ætatis Tertullianum jure dicendum arbitratur, Bibliothec. Scriptor. Theologiæ Moralis, pag. 27.
notes: §.III close: Oral as fundamental; Tertullian/Mayer; before §.IV.
